faq: What is the exact conversion factor?
1 nautical mile = 1.852 kilometres, exactly, by international definition since 1929. So nautical miles = kilometres ÷ 1.852, with no approximation in the factor itself.
Why do ships and aircraft use nautical miles?
Because a nautical mile is one minute of latitude — angles and distances share one scale on a chart. The Latitude Degrees to Nautical Miles page shows that geometry in full.
Is a nautical mile longer than a statute mile?
Yes: 1.852 km against about 1.609 km — roughly 15% longer. Confusing the two is the classic mixed-unit error this converter exists to prevent.
What is a knot in these units?
One knot is one nautical mile per hour. A vessel at 20 knots covers 37.04 km every hour — the conversion this page's factor produces.

How many nautical miles is a degree of latitude?
About 60.04 on the mean sphere — sixty by the arc-minute definition, with the small excess explained on the latitude conversion page.
